public_headline: United Airlines crew reported black UFO 100 feet from their Boeing 737
public_tldr: An FAA preliminary incident report records that the crew of United Airlines flight 1986, a Boeing 737-800 flying from San Francisco to Seattle, reported a black unidentified object roughly 100 feet from their aircraft at 8,000 feet altitude near Oakland, California. The document is a brief operations-centre log entry, not a full investigation, and includes no conclusions about what the object was.
public_narrative:
This document is a preliminary incident report from the FAA's Washington Operations Center, originally logged on 6 March 2024. It records a UAP (unidentified anomalous phenomena) sighting reported by the flight crew of United Airlines flight 1986, a Boeing 737-800 operating the San Francisco to Seattle route.

According to the report, the crew observed a black unidentified object approximately 100 feet from the aircraft's 1 o'clock position — that is, slightly to the right and ahead of the nose. At the time, the aircraft was heading northwest at 8,000 feet altitude, roughly 2 nautical miles north-northeast of Oakland, California (coordinates 37.75°N, 122.21°W). Despite the close proximity, the crew took no evasive action.

The report notes that law enforcement was not notified. The document carries an internal tracking reference (WOC 7-3333) and staff initials, but no follow-up investigation, analysis, or conclusion about the nature of the object is included. The only physical description given is the colour: black. No size, shape, speed, or behaviour of the object is recorded.

This is a single-page operational log entry — not a finished investigation or analytical product. It represents the earliest stage of FAA incident documentation: a crew report forwarded through the operations centre. Whether any further inquiry took place is not indicated in this document.
public_caveats: This is a preliminary operations-centre log, not a completed investigation or official finding. No conclusions about the object are drawn.
The account comes from a single source — the flight crew. No corroborating radar data, sensor readings, or independent witness reports are mentioned in the document.
The claimed 100-foot proximity at 8,000 feet altitude would represent a serious near-miss if accurate, but pilot distance estimates at altitude are inherently imprecise.
The only physical detail provided is the object's colour (black). No size, shape, speed, or flight behaviour is described.
No follow-up investigation is included in this document, so it is unknown whether additional inquiry was conducted.
